sentences.text: Stegosaurus is an extinct herbivorous dinosaur easily recognized by a double row of vertical kite-shaped plates on its back and two pairs of horizontal spikes at the tail's end.
This quadrupedal dinosaur possessed a long, narrow skull that was small relative to its body size.
Stegosaurus ungulatus is one of the largest stegosaurians, with specimens reaching about 9 meters in length and weighing over 6.9 metric tons.
Large Stegosaurus individuals could grow up to 9 meters long, 4 meters high, and weigh between 5.3 and 7 tons.
A well-preserved skull allowed Othniel Charles Marsh to create a brain mold in 1880.
The brain mold showed Stegosaurus had a very small brain, possibly the smallest among dinosaurs.
The genus Stegosaurus was first described by Othniel Charles Marsh in 1877 after he identified remains during the Bone Wars at Dinosaur Ridge National Landmark.
The initial fossils were found by Arthur Lakes and H.C. Beckwith north of Morrison, Colorado, at YPM Quarry 5.
Scientists generally agree that Stegosaurus used its spiked tails for defense and its plates primarily for display and secondarily for thermoregulation.
These defensive structures were likely vital for survival in the western United States and Portugal, where fossils date from 155 to 145 million years ago.
A large shoulder spike preserved in Stegosaurus sulcatus is speculated to be a key diagnostic feature for that species.
Stegosaurus lived alongside Apatosaurus, Diplodocus, Camarasaurus, and Allosaurus, which may have preyed on it.
Evidence of combat includes a punctured Allosaurus tail vertebra that fits perfectly with a Stegosaurus tail spike.
An Allosaurus specimen was killed when a Stegosaurus tail spike impaled its pubis, leading to a fatal infection.
A 2010 study by Mallison found support for a rearing posture in Kentrosaurus but not for the ability of its tail to act as a tripod.
The hypothesis that Stegosaurus could rear up on its hind legs was proposed by Bakker and opposed by Carpenter.
A 2009 study found that Stegosaurus plates and spikes grew more slowly than the rest of the skeleton until the animal reached maturity.
A 2022 study suggests Stegosaurus likely had an ectothermic or gigantothermic metabolism similar to modern reptiles.
The sacro-lumbar expansion found in Stegosaurus is a structure also present in birds and other ornithischians.
In birds, the sacro-lumbar expansion contains a glycogen body, a structure postulated to supply glycogen to the nervous system.
Shortly after describing Stegosaurus, Marsh observed an enlarged neural canal in the hip region that could have accommodated a structure up to 20 times larger than the brain.
Most known information about Stegosaurus comes from adult remains, though juvenile specimens have recently been found.
Senter (2026) presents evidence of a limited range of motion for the fingers of Stegosaurus.
The type species of the genus Stegosaurus is Stegosaurus stenops.
The International Commission on Zoological Nomenclature replaced the original type species with Stegosaurus stenops because the original type specimen was considered dubious.
Stegosaurus often falls within the subclade Stegosaurinae, which typically includes Wuerhosaurus and Hesperosaurus.
Stegosaurus lived during the Late Jurassic period, specifically from the Kimmeridgian to Tithonian stages.
Fossils have been found in the western United States and Portugal, dating from 155 to 145 million years ago.
A 2019 study suggests that the sister group to Stegosauria, Ankylosauria, may have originated in the early Early Jurassic based on fossil evidence from India.
Four different arrangements for the plates on Stegosaurus have been proposed over the years.
Frederick Lucas later changed his view to believe that Stegosaurus plates were attached in staggered rows.
